thread:
maria: quick heads-up — i'm going to prototype a feature-flagged permissions onramp for new tenants. goal: let teams opt into a simplified role flow before they hit full RBAC. thoughts?
ajay: 👍 makes sense. what's the minimal API surface you want? per-route overrides or just tenant-level presets?
maria: starting tenant-level presets + a lightweight override for routes we expose in the UI. avoid introducing a new entitlement schema if possible.
devon: careful about quotas — tenant presets could accidentally give wide route access that bypasses quota accounting. we need telemetry to show request counts by preset.
lina: agree. also add a flag that forces explicit consent for any preset that includes write scopes. UX can surface that at onboarding.
sam: from platform side, easiest is to store a "preset_id" on the tenant object and keep the existing role map. overrides can be a list of route_id -> allowed_actions, fall back to tenant preset. api change is small.
katie: rollout plan? canary to 5 tenants, collect metrics: errors, quota spikes, denied requests, and support tickets. also track how often people flip the preset off.
ajay: telemetry events i'd want: preset_applied, override_created, override_hit, permission_denied, quota_overflow. tag with tenant_id, actor, route, and rollout_flag.
maria: +1. devon — can we get a short dashboard tile in console showing preset adoption and top overridden routes?
devon: yes — we can add two panels: preset adoption over time and top 20 overrides by traffic. low effort if we reuse the routing telemetry pipeline.
sam: note: authz check path should short-circuit if preset grants access to avoid perf hit. that means we must ensure preset lookup is in the hot path cache.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag infra hook added to canary stack at 09:30 PST.
katie: small UX nit — when a preset grants access that could escalate, show a colored pill and a one-click audit view that expands the exact routes covered. helps support triage.
maria: agreed. last thing: migration story — existing tenants default to "strict" preset (no shortcuts) unless they opt-in. we'll include an email and in-console prompt. ok to start a spike tomorrow?
ajay: go for it. i'll take the API skeleton. devon will do telemetry panels. lina + katie will wire up the UX copy. sam will handle caching changes. i'll open a short RFC thread with proposed schema.
maria: thanks team. i'll post the spike PR when ready.
